input: Draft a daily evening shutdown routine for work

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The routine could cover just task wrap-up, or also include inbox triage, next-day planning, physical workspace tidying, and mental wind-down — knowing the boundaries shapes how long and detailed it is.
Whether the user works from home, in an office, or hybrid changes which steps are relevant — e.g., commute prep, shutting down a shared desk, or separating a home workspace mentally.
The total time available for the routine determines how many steps are realistic — a 10-minute routine looks very different from a 30-minute one.
If the routine needs to account for a team (e.g., sending end-of-day updates, handing off tasks) versus being purely personal, the steps and their order change significantly.
The tools the user relies on (e.g., Notion, paper journal, Slack, calendar) determine what a realistic and friction-free checklist actually looks like.
Knowing the user's biggest pain point — e.g., mentally switching off, feeling unfinished, morning chaos — reveals which outcome the routine must nail above all else.
Some people want a rigid, checklist-style routine; others prefer a loose, reflective wind-down. Tone and structure of the final output should match their natural working style.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a daily evening work shutdown routine
gold.taskDescription: Create a structured end-of-workday routine to help the user consistently close out their work day with intention and clarity.

questions.title: What specific activities should the routine cover?
questions.description: Determine the scope — e.g., task review, inbox triage, next-day planning, workspace tidy, mental wind-down — so nothing important is left out or over-included.

questions.title: Where do you work — home, office, or hybrid?
questions.description: Establish the physical work context so the routine steps are grounded in the user's actual environment.

questions.title: How many minutes can you realistically spend on this?
questions.description: Pin down the time budget so the routine is completable without feeling like a burden.

questions.title: Does the routine need to include team-facing steps?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user needs to send handoffs, status updates, or sign-off messages to colleagues as part of closing out.

questions.title: Which tools do you use to manage tasks and notes?
questions.description: Identify the specific apps or systems (e.g., Notion, paper planner, Slack, Google Calendar) so the routine integrates naturally with existing workflows.

questions.title: What is the biggest problem this routine needs to solve?
questions.description: Uncover the user's core pain point — such as inability to mentally switch off, chaotic mornings, or feeling unfinished — so the routine is designed around fixing it.

questions.title: Do you prefer a strict checklist or a flexible, reflective format?
questions.description: Understand the user's style preference so the final routine matches how they naturally like to work and wind down.
